utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, is there any need for a written response in the light of that? Or if there is, would you like to make the very quickly, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, thanks for that, Your Honour. I can say we'll review the transcript quickly and see if we have anything to add by way of a very quick written response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you will have a week from now to do that, so a response by next Wednesday. Because I think in light of what you say, it would be appropriate to hear also from the Registry on this if there are logistical issues arising. Now, Mr. Karadzic, in principle it seems that what you propose in this motion is not opposed by the Prosecution, but there may be issues of detail that need to be looked at and there may be the question of whether there are, in fact, resources on the part of the Victims and Witnesses Section to do what you ask. I will order the Victims and -- the Registry on behalf of Victims and Witnesses Section to make a submission under Rule 33(B) to the Trial Chamber in case there are any such issues. Meanwhile, in light of what's been said by Mr. Tieger, is there anything you wish to add?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I'd like to know whether this applies to 85 witnesses who will be testifying here viva voce, or does this relate to 92 bis witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's your application --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid I don't have it on me just now. Namely, I would like to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The application on the face of it relates to all witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have to say that 85 witnesses is not too many, that is, the ones that will be viva voce. As for interviewing 230 witnesses that the Prosecutor wishes to call under 92 bis, we're rather disturbed by such a large number of witnesses whose statements we will not hear. Because I come from a system in which the Prosecution does not work in the same way. This is done by the investigating judge, who is impartial and who collects what is good and what is bad for the Defence and presents the results. With all due respect, it is normal for the OTP to wish to succeed, not to mention conscious efforts to conceal something. We know of normal responses from Freud and others, and I can't -- I'm not quite sure that the Prosecution has taken things from the witnesses that are positive for the Defence. That is why we'd like to meet with them to make sure that nothing has been left out that might be favourable for the Defence; otherwise, the whole trial would give a rather poor image of itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So I now formally order the Registry to present a submission in response to this motion to advise the Chamber whether it presents any particular problems for Victims and Witnesses Section. I was just looking at the Rule there. I think it's an invitation I should extend rather than make an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that will be in keeping with what I said to Mr. Tieger, that will be by next Wednesday. I turn now to the third motion for adjudicated facts and a request by the Prosecution to reply to the accused's response on that. Now, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, is there a particular point that you wish to reply to? Because there are a number of tests to be considered when dealing with adjudicated facts, and your motion for leave to reply suggests that on something we might be misled by the material presented by the accused.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we actually only want to address in this reply two issues. The first issue is actually the accused's argument that it would be impermissible to take judicial notice of facts that were established based on documents rather than testimony. That is what we wanted to respond to because we think that's incorrect for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is his point not more that it's impermissible to take notice of the contents of document, which is rather different from saying it's impermissible to take notice of facts established on the basis of documents? There may be a confusion in the issue. I mean, what you say -- I can't see that there can be any doubt about what you say. And I don't think it's quite worded that way in the response.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, it's not worded in that way, but that is how we understood it because we are not actually providing adjudicated facts in relation to that there is something in a certain document. That we would definitely file differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I don't think you need to respond -- reply on that. What's the other point?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The other point is actually the order. The order -- motion for a list of witnesses to be eliminated. I think that's definitely something that we would like to oppose because there is at this moment not the proper time to withdraw any witnesses or give a list of witnesses that would be withdrawn should a fact -- fact be adjudicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is that matter of withdrawing names from the list of witnesses raised in the response to the motion?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Or is it raised in a separate --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's actually -- it's -- the response to the motion basically says response to the third Prosecution motion for adjudicated facts -- a notice of adjudicated facts and motion for list of witnesses to be eliminated. And it's actually at the -- at the end when the -- after the discussion on the various adjudicated facts on page 7, there is actually a request to order Prosecution to submit such a list. And we would oppose this because we can definitely not deal with this matter in the abstract, but rather need to see which adjudicated facts are granted. And then we would actually make such a submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I take it this reply is ready to be presented, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can -- I think we can do this tomorrow, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think you should reply on the latter point, and that is the question of adjusting the list of witnesses, but it's not necessary on the first one. And leave will formally be granted in the order that we ultimately make on the matter. Mr. Karadzic, that relates to your response to the third motion for adjudicated facts in which you've asked that the list of witnesses should be modified to the reflect the removal of witnesses who speak to the facts in which a decision on adjudication in favour of the Prosecution is made. It's only right that since you raise a quite separate matter in your response that the Prosecution should have the opportunity to reply to that. Their reply will be confined to that, and it will be done tomorrow. Now, you mentioned - and this is the last matter I have - you mentioned earlier today that you have a meeting later today - and I hope I'm not preventing it taking place - with representatives of the Registry about the arrangements for computerised access to electronic material. There's little I think that we can do on that matter today. I met with representatives of the Registry, as I indicated I would to you I think at the last Status Conference, to see what the situation was and what could be done. Now, as the result of my communications with them, they have identified certain measures which can be taken. And in light of that, they want to present these to you to see what can be done to satisfy your requirements. I'm sure you realise that there are certain limitations here, but as far as I can tell, efforts are being made to provide the maximum realistic access to material, particularly in the courtroom. I expect that any concerns you have you will try to resolve in direct communication with the Registry. If there are points that you think they're not taking a reasonable approach to, then I would expect you to ask them to refer these back to me. I'm quite happy to discuss further with a view to resolving this. I hope that we don't have to get involved in any formal determination of these issues. If the arrangements they have in mind are put in place, then this will be the extension -- a significant extension of developments which have already taken place in the Tribunal and in the Detention Unit to assist self-represented accused have access to material. But as I say, there are limitations on just how much assistance can be provided. So hopefully that will be resolved fairly soon and will not distract attention from the work necessary to prepare for the trial. Now, are there any other issues that you wish to raise with me today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. First of all, I'd like to say something in connection with the adjudicated facts. I'm expecting a translation of the second submission -- second notification which I should have received by the 6th of May and I haven't, the Serbian translation. I also agree with you, I see signs of goodwill by the Registry to assist me with these matters, so I hope that we will be able to resolve these issues without having to bother the Chamber. The people working on this are really people of goodwill, though certain rules for me are quite ununderstandable. Earlier on, people had laptops; and I don't need any wireless communication, but a laptop would come in very handy for me to bring with me here without having to leaf through my documents. I also wish to say that I have written 20-odd letters to certain governments asking them to provide me with relevant documents and evidence. This applies in the first place to failure to respect the arms embargo, then the illegal activities of certain national armed forces that used the UN as a Trojan horse, being present there and putting me -- putting us in a very bad position. And taking certain steps that are being treated here in an -- at a later stage, we will be asking from the signals intelligence data as to what certain governments did, and there will be some highly sensitive documents, and I will demand that the governments produce these. This trial cannot present the events that took place there -- I don't wish to defend only myself. Generals have been condemned here for things that our enemies carried out. They have been condemned to life imprisonment and 30 years' imprisonment for massacres committed by others, and we can prove this on conditions that the governments provide us with everything we have asked from them. So I appeal to you, not only with respect to governments but to non-governmental organisations, the United Nations, their agencies, and the International Red Cross. There were very strange things going on there, and I appeal to you to assist us if they do not respond to our request for the whole truth to be presented here. We use the term the bare truth, the naked truth, and -- which means that the truth does not have the colours of the interested parties. There is one truth and that truth should not have a banner on it, but it should be completely clear and naked. These are the things that we will be working on. These letters have already been sent. The first group of letters for the most innocent matters like failure to respect the embargo. But I fear that we will meet with the obstruction of many governments regarding the provision of documents about the events in Bosnia, as these will be very sensitive issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: While you were speaking there I was told that the second Prosecution motion for judicial notice of adjudicated facts will be ready on the 16th of June in B/C/S. I can't remember now what date we anticipated it, but you will remember that we postponed your response --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 6th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think you said the 6th of May, did you? Or did you mean the 6th of -- 6th of May?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The translation was expected on the 6th of May. That was what it was announced, but I didn't receive it then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, it will be ready on the 16th of June. The date we fixed before for your response, I think, was the 30th of June. I think it appropriate to extend that period in light of the date for the translation, and instead of the 30th of June, I now fix the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just say also, though this perhaps is not something that is dealt with by your Chamber, that is very difficult with the funds given by the Registry to keep certain experts working on this trial at the rates given to assistant staff. As for what I said about unconscious notifications, this applies also to Judge Picard. I'm not saying that she would consciously -- I'm talking about unconscious motivations, or subconscious motivations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the issue relating to Judge Picard is one which has been dealt with and which is now the subject of appeal, so I think you should deal with that matter in the course of the appeal process.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted you to know that this is not personal, nor am I accusing anyone of any conscious action but something subconscious that one has no control of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tieger, is there anything else that the Prosecution wish to say today?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, that completes this Status Conference. As I said earlier, the next one will be on the 1st of July, and I think it's in the morning, is it? Yeah, it will be at 10.00 a.m. on the 1st of July. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: adjourned at 5.00 p.m.
